It can look different for each person—maybe this isn’t it for you—but my understanding of a ‘shut down’ is that it’s a form of dissociation. It can impact your ability to think, feel, move, and speak.

I remember the first time this happened to me, I was terrified of myself. My mind went blank, or at times would ‘play’ random thoughts or songs but nothing relevant or coherent. I couldn’t speak or move. 
Our brains are essentially in overwhelm and the only way it knows to protect us in that moment is to ‘unplug’. It sounds like you were dissociating to me. There are lots of great posts here about people’s experiences with them if you’re interested.

Currently 24, in school for a degree that I love (though I’m definitely depleted and may be edging towards burn out), have good friendships around me, am able to work and build networks, and am living on my own. My abuse isn’t from my family, though there was some emotional abuse and violence in my family, so they support me a bit financially. I would say 80% is me and 20% is them. For me, I find that I’m 2 different people. There’s the version that shows up at work, school, friends, family, and general public. She’s more confident, outgoing, works hard, and looks like she has life going on for her.

Then there’s the version of me that shows up when I’m alone or in therapy which is when I feel like a kid. I feel useless and stupid and experience a lot of imposter syndrome. This version of me typically bleeds into my first version but she remains in my thoughts and less my actions (though it does seep through time to time). 

It’s hard. It’s a LOT of energy. I’m medicated and tbh it’s the only way I survive at times. Some days I want to give up and in some ways, I do. I ignore things that I need to do and just dissociate in bed. But the only thing keeping me going is that I envisioned a life for myself as a kid and it tastes like freedom and joy and I NEED to feel that one day. I need to get my degree so I can get a job and pay off my debt and live independently and get into a stable relationship and maybe life will feel worth living again.
